ROOT: COUPLED NONCRITICAL PHYSICAL-SHEAR DECAY AND AN EFFECTIVE CERTIFICATE
10 November 2026 Brisbane. Scope: the actual LINEAR viscous Rayleigh-Squire system on a fixed noncritical fibre. This is not the nonlinear common-body-force compiler.

INPUT/OPERATORS. Fix integers p!=0,l with r^2=p^2+l^2>=2, positive rational nu,T and rational0<delta<1. Put kappa=2pi, D_m=r^2+m^2, q_m=1-1/D_m, Q=diag(q_m), z=sqrt(Q)D V, zeta=kappa*i*(l*v1-p*v3). The physical cosine shear is b=A*cos(kappa*x2)*e1. In H=l2(Z) directsum l2(Z),
 d(z,zeta)/dt=(-Gamma+B_A)(z,zeta),
 Gamma=diag(kappa^2*nu*D,kappa^2*nu*D),
 B_A=[-i*kappa*p*A*J,0; A*C,-i*kappa*p*A*J0],
 J_(m,m+1)=sqrt(q_m*q_(m+1))/2,
 (J0)_(m,m+1)=1/2,
 C=2pi^2*l*(S-S^-1)*D^-1*Q^-1/2.
All offdiagonal operators are bounded, with band width1; q>=1/2. A computable rational b_A>=||B_A|| follows from shift norms, r^2>=2, pi<4 and sqrt2<2. Irrational entries are enclosed, not supplied as free exact reals.

GOVERNING EXISTING COUPLED ESTIMATE. ROOT reread Li-Wei-Zhang arXiv1801.05645v1 (the current sole version), equations1.5-1.7 and Theorem1.1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.05645v1 . The theorem includes the FORCED Squire block, not just its homogeneous part. In its noncritical regime it bounds phi by C*exp(-a*t)*||phi0|| and omega2 by C*exp(-a*t)*||omega20||+C*|p|^-1*(1+a*t)*exp(-a*t)*||phi0||, where a=c3*sqrt(|p*gamma|)+nu'*(p^2+l^2), assuming nu'<c2*sqrt(|gamma|). Its separate nonlinear theorem has additional restrictions and is not imported here.

EXACT RESCALING. Set X=kappa*x and translate the transverse coordinate by a quarter period. Keep physical t unchanged. Then nu'=kappa^2*nu, shear amplitude in the paper's equation is kappa*A, k_f=1 and gamma=kappa^3*nu*A. The paper's phi=Delta_X v2=-D V=-Q^-1/2*z, and omega2=zeta/kappa. These fixed norm equivalences are bounded on the present fibre. For sufficiently large integer A, the theorem's viscosity condition holds and a->infinity. Consequently
 ||exp[T*(-Gamma+B_A)]||_(H->H) -> 0 as A->infinity.
In particular the A-prefactored offdiagonal Duhamel block in E104 tends to zero. No inference from the two separate diagonal decay limits is used; the coupled estimate supplies precisely that missing statement. This imports existing mathematics, not a new scattering theorem or a first-weighted-moment Jacobi result.
